From: Allen Nguyen <allen.nguyen@quantumbridge.com>

Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation: pricing and surge protection

Markus / Camila —

Quick context: our renewal for next year lands in July. Usage has climbed faster than expected (esp. inference calls for our customer support bot) and Finance is pushing us to lock unit economics before we commit. We need a short-term bridge proposal while we finalize an expanded commit — specifically: a temporary price hold for current rates through Q4, a tiered discount for a 12-month commit, and a modest surge credit for unexpected spikes during the first 90 days.

Can Redwood share an updated concession matrix (tier discounts, burst credits, price-hold end date) and a short ops plan for how capacity will be guaranteed during peak events? Need to present to our procurement + legal by next Tuesday (May 10).

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

Allen
Allen Nguyen
Head of Cloud Ops, QuantumBridge

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Allen Nguyen <allen.nguyen@quantumbridge.com>, Priya Bose <priya.bose@quantumbridge.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: pricing and surge protection

Allen / Priya —

Thanks for the context and the snapshot. We can definitely put a concise package together for procurement/legal. Attached is a first-pass concession matrix (renewal_concession_matrix_v2.xlsx) plus a short implementation runbook draft for ops handoff. High-level summary in case you need a one-pager for legal: 

- Price-hold: Maintain existing unit rate through 2027-10-31 if customer signs a 12-month committed plan by 2027-05-20.
- Commit tiers: 3 thresholds (Base / Growth / Scale) with volume discounts of 10% / 18% / 26% applied to inference tokens after the baseline.
- Surge credit: One-time 90-day surge buffer equal to 10% of monthly committed capacity, applicable for usage spikes above 120% of average monthly consumption in Q2. Credits applied as invoice-level offsets, capped at 2 months of baseline spend.
- Implementation: We propose a canary burst pool + prefix KV caching enabled on day one of the new term; runbook attached describes routing, escalation, and rollback steps.

If that looks OK I can pull approvals for the price-hold and the surge credit with Sales Ops today. A couple items we need from you to finalize: confirmed baseline (monthly committed tokens), legal + procurement preferred sign-by date (you noted May 10; we recommend May 20 to allow internal approvals), and whether you want the surge credit to be automatic or require Ops request to trigger.

Next steps (if you approve): I’ll route the concession matrix to Pricing for formal sign-off, and loop in Lauren for a short SLA/credit memo.

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Renewals — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Attachment: renewal_concession_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx), implementation_runbook_draft.md (md)

Folks — forwarding Allen's ask + my draft matrix. Fast alignment needed: QuantumBridge (QB-4529) wants a price-hold plus an introductory surge credit for their renewal. High level is above; see attachments.

Specific asks for this thread: 
- Lauren: can you review the discount ladder and confirm we can approve the 26% top-tier discount under the proposed Commit terms, or suggest a staged step-up instead? Also please confirm whether the invoice-offset approach for surge credits triggers any billing system limitations.
- Camila: ops review of the runbook — will the canary burst pool + KV caching plan meet their 90-day surge window? Anything missing from escalation runbook (contacts, on-call rotation, monitoring thresholds)?

I want to be ready to send a formal package to Allen by end-of-day Wednesday. Low-friction approval path preferred — if Pricing needs a one-off waiver, flag it and I’ll route to Finance.

Onward —
Markus

Allen / Priya —

Appreciate the patience while we pulled approvals. Please see the agreed terms below and attached concession matrix + a short ops runbook for Q2->Q3 transition. We recommend capturing these via an amendment and a DocuSign link (included).

Agreed commercial summary (conditional on signed 12-month commit):
- Price-hold: Current unit rates held through 2027-10-31 if signed by 2027-05-20.
- Commit tiers (applied to monthly committed tokens):
  * Base (Up to X tokens): no discount (status quo)
  * Growth (X+1 to Y tokens): 18% discount
  * Scale (Y+1+ tokens): 26% discount
- Surge credit: 10% of monthly committed capacity available as a one-time 90-day buffer. Credit applies automatically if monthly consumption > 120% of Q2 average, capped at two months' baseline spend.
- Implementation commitments: Redwood will provision a canary burst pool, enable prefix-level KV caching, and run a pre-cutover soak test. Detailed runbook attached; our SRE on-call (Camila) will be primary escalation for the first 30 days.

Operational notes: please confirm your baseline numbers (monthly committed tokens) and whether your procurement/legal wants the invoice-offset surge credit or a separate credit memo. For DocuSign, we will generate an amendment referencing QB-4529 and the attached concession matrix; turnaround target is 72 hours once we receive signed baseline numbers.

Links & attachments: concession matrix (renewal_concession_matrix_v2.xlsx), implementation runbook (implementation_runbook_draft.md), DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/ds/boards/XYZ-12345

If this aligns, please reply with: 1) confirmed baseline figure, 2) sign-by authorisation (who signs on your side), and 3) whether surge credits should be automatic. I’ll open the DocuSign and loop in Finance for final invoicing notes.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this quickly.
